#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE — WEEKEND EDITION | NOV 7 ⚡

The Nasdaq fell 5.5% Thursday after the U.S. midterms. Then Friday’s payrolls came in at +165K vs. +65K expected, sending the dollar and yields higher. Markets ended the week pricing roughly an 80% chance of a December Fed hike.

☢️ URANIUM
TradeTech reported a record $99/lb long-term indicator, with spot near $92 on Friday. Two U.S. utilities signed for 1.1M lb from UEC through 2032 at prevailing spot prices on delivery. On the supply side, Kazatomprom reported Q3 output up 12% year over year on a 100% basis.

🥈 SILVER
Spot jumped 5.7% on the week to $51.94/oz after ending October below $50. Thursday’s interim review is the next test for April’s 46.3M oz deficit forecast.

🟠 COPPER
LME three-month copper fell 3.3% to $13,780/t as the AI trade unwound. Meanwhile, China’s Yangshan import premium hit a record $210/t and Codelco cut its 2026 output outlook to just over 1.2M tonnes. Physical buyers in China are paying up even as futures sell off.

🥇 GOLD
Spot gained 5% on the week to about $4,071/oz despite Friday’s pullback. The World Gold Council reported 321 tonnes of net central-bank buying in Q3, up 42% year over year. Global gold ETFs took in another $2.7B in October.

👀 NEXT WEEK | NOV 9–13

Mon — China CPI and PPI. COP31 opens in Türkiye.
Tue — U.S. CPI, China trade data and NexGen’s Rook I update.
Thu — Metals Focus presents its interim silver findings.
Fri — U.S. PPI.

Tuesday’s CPI is the big test for gold and silver. A softer print could take some pressure off yields. I’m also watching oil after fresh strikes near Hormuz, and whether China’s copper premiums stay elevated if tech stocks slide again.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the next Daily Metals Pulse.

tweets.text:
If you’re looking for a year-end trade, look no further.

The $VIX has already spiked to around 27. If it reaches 30, I believe you’ll have the last great trade of the year on your hands.

A $VIX of 30 is not sustainable indefinitely. A market drawdown, by its very nature, reduces the risk of the next drawdown as stocks become cheaper, especially when corporate earnings continue to rise.

Seasonality has played out almost perfectly. And the higher volatility spikes, the faster I expect it to collapse.

If the $VIX approaches 30 over the next few days, I believe shorting $UVXY or $UVIX could be one of the best trades for the next four months.

My expected return is 30% to 50% over the next four months.

If you want to be more cautious, you can wait for a potential U.S. attack on Iran. If that happens, I would look to put this trade on the same day, assuming volatility spikes accordingly.

I would structure the trade using options, selling far out-of-the-money calls to finance the purchase of near-the-money puts, while also selling two or three far out-of-the-money puts to reduce the cost further.

I would be happy to get assigned a short position in $UVXY if the short calls are exercised, as that would likely mean the $VIX has moved well above 30.

Position sizing is key here. Position sizing is also your risk management.

The problem with shorting VIX futures is that you eventually have to roll them, and the longer-dated futures won’t give you the same bang for your buck.

In contrast, instruments like $VXX and $UVXY are structurally designed to lose value over time, particularly when the futures curve is in contango.

You want to bet against the house over time, not just for a day, a week, or a month. These instruments allow you to do exactly that.

tweets.text:
Wanted to expand on the graduation point from my last Elys post

imo tokens launched on @Enter_Elysium have a shot at the full HL lifecycle:

onchain → HL spot → HL perps

e.g. on RH chain most protocols want to get listed on the RH app as a form of validation. On Elys tho, the next step up is HL itself. huge distro perk for builders

rn most of the launches are happening on @MontraXYZ 

as with every new chain, the first and fiercest battleground is... you guessed it, the launchpads lol

using data from elysa terminal:

> ~65% of launchpad volume in the last hr, ~62% over 24h (vs ~27% all time, so flow is rotating in)
> ~66% of new tokens in the last hr, 11K of 18.6K in the last 24h
> $EACCAT is the biggest trending token at ~$4.4M on Montra,  followed by $BLOB at ~$2.7M on Elyspump and $CHAMELEON at ~$2.2M on Montra
> 3 of the top 5 trending are Montra launches
> ~20 launchpads on the chain rn and Montra is doing ~2/3 of the flow before mainnet goes live Nov 9

will be interesting to see if they can hold the lead going into mainnet, but the flow dominance so far (volume traded, tokens launched, highest mcap coins) is a strong start

anw tech wise, the pad has one uni v4 pool per token, no migration + fee sits in the pool not the token. protocol cut buys back $MONTRA via the kinetiq:native pair, so it depends on volume holding up after TGE (the rev buybacks and xRev narrative here will be one to watch again)

interesting spot to consider from the Elys onchain -> HL spot/perps lifecycle narrative, and imo the tokens with the best narratives will stand the best chance at doing so (i.e. $CASHCAT listing on RH few weeks into chain going live)
tweets.quoted_tweet_text: +the graduation from onchain to HL spot + perps listing is also another distro perk

tweets.text:
1/ Use a coding harness: Codex, Code claude, Copilot CLI, it doesn't matter.
2/ Download an architecture software. In my case, my architect is using Vector works but you can use ArchiCAD, AutoCAD etc. It's best if they have an API so it can be used programmatically. 
3/ then ask your coding harness to connect and use it programmatically. If the API fails, worse case GPT models are very good at computer use. It will just be slower.
